findings.title: Add a LICENSE; redistribution rights are undefined
findings.evidence: no licence file at the repository root
findings.why: With no licence the default is all rights reserved, so this code cannot legally be reused, which matters most for the owner's own work carried into client engagements.
findings.fix: Add MIT or Apache-2.0 at the repository root.

findings.title: Add a workflow that builds and tests this repository
findings.why: Every change merges with nobody having run the build once, which across this estate is 499 repositories.
findings.fix: Add a workflow running the project build and test command on push and pull_request.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Strip notebook outputs before committing
findings.evidence: 28 notebook(s) over 1MB, 68.5MB total, dominated by stored output
findings.why: Outputs are where a printed dataframe of customer rows or a traceback containing a connection string ends up, and diff review never reads them.
findings.fix: Install nbstripout and clear the existing outputs once.

findings.title: Split the oversized notebook cell into steps
findings.evidence: largest cell 4268 characters of 17562 (3 notebooks sampled)
findings.why: A failure anywhere in a 22,000-character cell means rerunning the whole pipeline from load to model, so nothing can be debugged in isolation.
findings.fix: Break at the load, clean, feature, model and evaluate boundaries.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image

findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs

findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a critical advisory
findings.why: The manifest pins the exact version the advisory covers, so this is not a warning about drift: the vulnerable code is what installs, and a critical rating means it is reachable over the network without credentials or user interaction.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Add a LICENSE; redistribution rights are undefined
findings.evidence: no licence file at the repository root
findings.why: With no licence the default is all rights reserved, so this code cannot legally be reused, which matters most for the owner's own work carried into client engagements.
findings.fix: Add MIT or Apache-2.0 at the repository root.

findings.fix: Add one test per public entry point, then a CI step that runs them.

findings.fix: Add tests for the highest fan-in modules first.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Remove the committed .env and rotate what it holds
findings.why: A tracked .env is the most common route for a working key to reach a public clone, and it is the file the app actually loads, so the value is usually live.
findings.fix: git rm --cached the file, add it to .gitignore, rotate every credential it names, commit a .env.example with empty values.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 1 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 1 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Add a pre-commit secret gate
findings.evidence: a secret-shaped file is tracked and no repo-level gate is visible
findings.why: Without a gate the same class of leak recurs on the next commit, so a leak finding is the symptom and this is the cause.
findings.fix: Add a pre-commit hook scanning staged content, and enable push protection.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA

findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Add a test suite; this repository has none
findings.why: Any change ships with no signal that existing behaviour still holds, so a regression reaches production undetected.

findings.why: Every change merges with nobody having run the build once, which across this estate is 499 repositories.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Commit a lockfile beside the manifest
findings.evidence: manifest with no lockfile in scope
findings.why: An unlocked range means the artifact you tested and the artifact you ship can contain different transitive code, so a malicious patch release reaches production with no diff.
findings.fix: Run the package manager once and commit the generated lockfile.

findings.title: Remove eval over a runtime value
findings.why: eval executes whatever the string contains, so wherever that string came from is now able to run code in the process, and the distance between the input and the eval is usually the only thing making it look safe.
findings.fix: Parse the value into the type you expect, with json.loads or ast.literal_eval.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 1 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 1 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate

findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Make CI invoke the test suite it has
findings.evidence: 4 test files, no test command in the 4 workflows read
findings.why: A green check that never executed an assertion is worse than no check, because reviewers trust it.
findings.fix: Add a test step to the existing workflow rather than a new workflow.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository
findings.why: One repository here carries twenty blobs over 5MB including a 10.9MB spreadsheet, so every clone and every CI checkout pays for data nobody diffs.
findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a critical advisory
findings.evidence: gradio@5.50.0 CVE-2026-27167 (critical) +12 more; ray@2.53.0 CVE-2026-27482 (critical) +5 more
findings.why: The manifest pins the exact version the advisory covers, so this is not a warning about drift: the vulnerable code is what installs, and a critical rating means it is reachable over the network without credentials or user interaction.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Make CI invoke the test suite it has
findings.evidence: 28 test files, no test command in the 4 workflows read
findings.why: A green check that never executed an assertion is worse than no check, because reviewers trust it.
findings.fix: Add a test step to the existing workflow rather than a new workflow.

findings.title: Open a pull request instead of pushing to the default branch
findings.why: Automated commits land on the branch that deploys, with no test having run against the result.
findings.fix: Push to a bot branch and open a pull request, or restrict the push to a tag ref.

findings.title: Stop passing the secret as a build argument or image env
findings.evidence: ENV SYNTHESIZER_API_KEY with a baked value
findings.why: ARG and ENV values are recorded in the image layers, so the credential is readable with docker history by anyone who can pull the image, and deleting the file in a later layer does not remove it.
findings.fix: Mount it at build time with --mount=type=secret, or inject it at run time.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 4 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 2 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Add a test suite; this repository has none
findings.why: Any change ships with no signal that existing behaviour still holds, so a regression reaches production undetected.
findings.fix: Add one test per public entry point, then a CI step that runs them.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 1 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 1 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.fix: Move secret-using steps into a workflow_run job that never checks out pull request code, or gate on an environment with required reviewers.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Open a pull request instead of pushing to the default branch
findings.why: Automated commits land on the branch that deploys, with no test having run against the result.
findings.fix: Push to a bot branch and open a pull request, or restrict the push to a tag ref.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA

findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Replace the wildcard CORS origin with an explicit allow list

findings.title: Turn off debug mode and drive it from the environment

findings.fix: Delete continue-on-error, or move a genuinely advisory step into a separate non-required job.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 2 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 2 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Remove eval over a runtime value
findings.why: eval executes whatever the string contains, so wherever that string came from is now able to run code in the process, and the distance between the input and the eval is usually the only thing making it look safe.
findings.fix: Parse the value into the type you expect, with json.loads or ast.literal_eval.

findings.title: Replace the wildcard CORS origin with an explicit allow list
findings.why: Any page on the internet can call the API with the browser's cookies attached, so a logged-in visitor to an unrelated site performs authenticated requests without knowing, and the wildcard combined with credentials is the exact configuration browsers refuse for that reason.
findings.fix: List the origins the API actually serves, and never pair a wildcard with credentials.

findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Keep secrets out of workflows a fork can trigger
findings.why: Contributor-controlled input reaches a job holding a publish token or cloud credential, so a pull request becomes credential exfiltration.
findings.fix: Move secret-using steps into a workflow_run job that never checks out pull request code, or gate on an environment with required reviewers.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a published advisory
findings.evidence: axios@1.12.2 CVE-2026-44494 (high) +27 more; vite@7.2.6 CVE-2026-53571 (high) +4 more; uuid@13.0.0 CVE-2026-41907 (medium)
findings.why: The pinned version is the one that installs, so a published advisory against it describes this deployment rather than a hypothetical one, and the advisory is also a public description of how to exploit it.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Make CI invoke the test suite it has
findings.evidence: 93 test files, no test command in any workflow
findings.why: A green check that never executed an assertion is worse than no check, because reviewers trust it.
findings.fix: Add a test step to the existing workflow rather than a new workflow.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 3 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 2 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Install from the lockfile in CI
findings.evidence: npm install with a committed package-lock.json
findings.why: A fresh resolution in CI means the tested dependency set is not the locked one, so the failure only appears after merge.
findings.fix: Use npm ci, yarn install --immutable, or pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Untrack the file your own .gitignore says to ignore
findings.why: The author already decided this file must never be committed, so its presence is an accident nobody noticed, which means the credentials in it are the ones actually in use.

findings.title: Remove the committed .env and rotate what it holds
findings.why: A tracked .env is the most common route for a working key to reach a public clone, and it is the file the app actually loads, so the value is usually live.
findings.fix: git rm --cached the file, add it to .gitignore, rotate every credential it names, commit a .env.example with empty values.

findings.fix: List the origins the API actually serves, and never pair a wildcard with credentials.

findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Add a test suite; this repository has none
findings.why: Any change ships with no signal that existing behaviour still holds, so a regression reaches production undetected.
findings.fix: Add one test per public entry point, then a CI step that runs them.

findings.title: Make CI invoke the test suite it has
findings.evidence: 504 test files, no test command in any workflow
findings.why: A green check that never executed an assertion is worse than no check, because reviewers trust it.
findings.fix: Add a test step to the existing workflow rather than a new workflow.

findings.title: Remove continue-on-error from steps that gate correctness
findings.why: A failing test suite reports a green check, which is precisely the path this audit exists to close.
findings.fix: Delete continue-on-error, or move a genuinely advisory step into a separate non-required job.

findings.title: Open a pull request instead of pushing to the default branch
findings.why: Automated commits land on the branch that deploys, with no test having run against the result.
findings.fix: Push to a bot branch and open a pull request, or restrict the push to a tag ref.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan

findings.title: Remove generated build output from version control

findings.title: Add a LICENSE; redistribution rights are undefined
findings.evidence: no licence file at the repository root
findings.why: With no licence the default is all rights reserved, so this code cannot legally be reused, which matters most for the owner's own work carried into client engagements.

findings.title: Commit a lockfile beside the manifest
findings.evidence: manifest with no lockfile in scope
findings.why: An unlocked range means the artifact you tested and the artifact you ship can contain different transitive code, so a malicious patch release reaches production with no diff.
findings.fix: Run the package manager once and commit the generated lockfile.

findings.title: Re-enable certificate verification
findings.why: With verification off the connection is encrypted to whoever answered, which is no protection at all: anyone positioned between the two hosts can present their own certificate, read the traffic and alter it, and the request will still succeed.
findings.fix: Remove the flag, and if the peer uses a private CA point the client at that CA bundle instead.

findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Expand the test suite; it cannot cover this codebase
findings.why: A reviewer reads "has tests" and assumes a safety net that covers two files out of eighty-five, which is how untested paths ship behind a green badge.
findings.fix: Add tests for the highest fan-in modules first.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository
findings.why: One repository here carries twenty blobs over 5MB including a 10.9MB spreadsheet, so every clone and every CI checkout pays for data nobody diffs.
findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Rotate the credentials in the committed environment file
findings.why: These values are loaded by the application at boot, so a generated value here is a working credential for something that runs.
findings.fix: Rotate each named credential, remove the file from the index, and replace it with a keys-only example.

findings.title: Untrack the file your own .gitignore says to ignore
findings.why: The author already decided this file must never be committed, so its presence is an accident nobody noticed, which means the credentials in it are the ones actually in use.
findings.fix: git rm --cached the path and rotate; the ignore rule is already correct.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a published advisory
findings.evidence: github.com/xuri/excelize/v2@2.10.0 CVE-2026-54063 (high) +1 more; go.opentelemetry.io/otel@1.40.0 CVE-2026-29181 (high) +1 more; go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk@1.40.0 CVE-2026-39883 (high) +1 more; github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4@4.1.3 CVE-2026-34986 (high) +1 more; and 1 more package(s)
findings.why: The pinned version is the one that installs, so a published advisory against it describes this deployment rather than a hypothetical one, and the advisory is also a public description of how to exploit it.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Remove the committed .env and rotate what it holds
findings.why: A tracked .env is the most common route for a working key to reach a public clone, and it is the file the app actually loads, so the value is usually live.
findings.fix: git rm --cached the file, add it to .gitignore, rotate every credential it names, commit a .env.example with empty values.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 1 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 1 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Remove the committed .env and rotate what it holds
findings.why: A tracked .env is the most common route for a working key to reach a public clone, and it is the file the app actually loads, so the value is usually live.
findings.fix: git rm --cached the file, add it to .gitignore, rotate every credential it names, commit a .env.example with empty values.

findings.title: Open a pull request instead of pushing to the default branch
findings.why: Automated commits land on the branch that deploys, with no test having run against the result.
findings.fix: Push to a bot branch and open a pull request, or restrict the push to a tag ref.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Install from the lockfile in CI
findings.why: A fresh resolution in CI means the tested dependency set is not the locked one, so the failure only appears after merge.
findings.fix: Use npm ci, yarn install --immutable, or pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Add a pre-commit secret gate
findings.evidence: a secret-shaped file is tracked and no repo-level gate is visible
findings.why: Without a gate the same class of leak recurs on the next commit, so a leak finding is the symptom and this is the cause.
findings.fix: Add a pre-commit hook scanning staged content, and enable push protection.

findings.title: Expand the test suite; it cannot cover this codebase
findings.why: A reviewer reads "has tests" and assumes a safety net that covers two files out of eighty-five, which is how untested paths ship behind a green badge.
findings.fix: Add tests for the highest fan-in modules first.

findings.why: With no licence the default is all rights reserved, so this code cannot legally be reused, which matters most for the owner's own work carried into client engagements.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image

findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.

findings.why: An unlocked range means the artifact you tested and the artifact you ship can contain different transitive code, so a malicious patch release reaches production with no diff.
findings.fix: Run the package manager once and commit the generated lockfile.

findings.title: Make CI invoke the test suite it has
findings.evidence: 12 test files, no test command in any workflow
findings.why: A green check that never executed an assertion is worse than no check, because reviewers trust it.
findings.fix: Add a test step to the existing workflow rather than a new workflow.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add a test suite; this repository has none
findings.why: Any change ships with no signal that existing behaviour still holds, so a regression reaches production undetected.
findings.fix: Add one test per public entry point, then a CI step that runs them.

findings.title: Add a workflow that builds and tests this repository
findings.why: Every change merges with nobody having run the build once, which across this estate is 499 repositories.
findings.fix: Add a workflow running the project build and test command on push and pull_request.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA

findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a published advisory
findings.evidence: python-multipart@0.0.6 CVE-2024-24762 (high) +17 more; fastapi@0.104.1 CVE-2024-24762 (high); jinja2@3.1.2 CVE-2024-56201 (high) +9 more

findings.title: Drop privileged mode and host networking

findings.fix: git rm --cached the file, add it to .gitignore, rotate every credential it names, commit a .env.example with empty values.

findings.why: An unlocked range means the artifact you tested and the artifact you ship can contain different transitive code, so a malicious patch release reaches production with no diff.
findings.fix: Run the package manager once and commit the generated lockfile.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Stop discarding the exit code of steps whose failure matters
findings.why: The job reports green while the artifact it was supposed to produce was never produced, so a crash becomes a successful run built on stale data.
findings.fix: Let the step fail, or test the specific expected condition instead of discarding all exit codes.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate

findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository
findings.why: One repository here carries twenty blobs over 5MB including a 10.9MB spreadsheet, so every clone and every CI checkout pays for data nobody diffs.
findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Review the install lifecycle script and disable scripts in CI
findings.why: Install scripts are the execution vector for every npm compromise from event-stream onward, and a postinstall that fetches a binary makes the build depend on a URL nobody reviews.
findings.fix: Move the work into an explicit build step, or set ignore-scripts in CI and run it by name.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Replace the wildcard CORS origin with an explicit allow list
findings.why: Any page on the internet can call the API with the browser's cookies attached, so a logged-in visitor to an unrelated site performs authenticated requests without knowing, and the wildcard combined with credentials is the exact configuration browsers refuse for that reason.
findings.fix: List the origins the API actually serves, and never pair a wildcard with credentials.

findings.title: Remove eval over a runtime value
findings.why: eval executes whatever the string contains, so wherever that string came from is now able to run code in the process, and the distance between the input and the eval is usually the only thing making it look safe.
findings.fix: Parse the value into the type you expect, with json.loads or ast.literal_eval.

findings.title: Pass the command as a list instead of building a shell string
findings.evidence: os.system with an interpolated command string
findings.why: With shell=True the string is parsed by a shell, so a semicolon or a backtick anywhere in an interpolated value runs a second command with the process's privileges, and the interpolation is what makes it reachable from input.
findings.fix: Drop shell=True and pass an argument list, so the values can never be read as syntax.

findings.fix: Use yaml.safe_load, or JSON, and for model weights prefer a format that does not carry code.

findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Add a pre-commit secret gate
findings.evidence: a secret-shaped file is tracked and no repo-level gate is visible
findings.why: Without a gate the same class of leak recurs on the next commit, so a leak finding is the symptom and this is the cause.
findings.fix: Add a pre-commit hook scanning staged content, and enable push protection.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository
findings.why: One repository here carries twenty blobs over 5MB including a 10.9MB spreadsheet, so every clone and every CI checkout pays for data nobody diffs.
findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Review the install lifecycle script and disable scripts in CI
findings.why: Install scripts are the execution vector for every npm compromise from event-stream onward, and a postinstall that fetches a binary makes the build depend on a URL nobody reviews.
findings.fix: Move the work into an explicit build step, or set ignore-scripts in CI and run it by name.

findings.title: Expand the test suite; it cannot cover this codebase
findings.why: A reviewer reads "has tests" and assumes a safety net that covers two files out of eighty-five, which is how untested paths ship behind a green badge.
findings.fix: Add tests for the highest fan-in modules first.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Add a test suite; this repository has none
findings.why: Any change ships with no signal that existing behaviour still holds, so a regression reaches production undetected.
findings.fix: Add one test per public entry point, then a CI step that runs them.

findings.title: Add a workflow that builds and tests this repository
findings.why: Every change merges with nobody having run the build once, which across this estate is 499 repositories.
findings.fix: Add a workflow running the project build and test command on push and pull_request.

findings.title: Add a build gate for the deployable artifacts here
findings.why: Something in the repo is meant to reach a server and no automated step has ever validated it, which is the state of 125 repositories here.
findings.fix: Add a workflow that at least builds the image and validates the manifests.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 4 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 3 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a critical advisory
findings.evidence: pillow@12.1.1 CVE-2026-59198 (critical) +35 more; pyjwt@2.10.1 CVE-2025-45768 (critical) +12 more; cryptography@46.0.5 CVE-2026-39892 (critical) +10 more
findings.why: The manifest pins the exact version the advisory covers, so this is not a warning about drift: the vulnerable code is what installs, and a critical rating means it is reachable over the network without credentials or user interaction.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a published advisory
findings.evidence: aiohttp@3.13.3 CVE-2026-69244 (high) +47 more; requests@2.32.5 CVE-2026-25645 (medium) +1 more; uv@0.10.6 GHSA-4gg8-gxpx-9rph (medium) +1 more; zeroconf@0.148.0 CVE-2026-48045 (medium) +9 more
findings.why: The pinned version is the one that installs, so a published advisory against it describes this deployment rather than a hypothetical one, and the advisory is also a public description of how to exploit it.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Commit a lockfile beside the manifest
findings.evidence: manifest with no lockfile in scope
findings.why: An unlocked range means the artifact you tested and the artifact you ship can contain different transitive code, so a malicious patch release reaches production with no diff.
findings.fix: Run the package manager once and commit the generated lockfile.

findings.title: Pin the resolution so a vulnerable version cannot install
findings.evidence: no lockfile, and the declared ranges reach certifi@2021.5.30 CVE-2023-37920 (high) +5 more; urllib3@2.0 CVE-2025-66471 (high) +15 more
findings.why: The range includes versions with published advisories and nothing in the repository records which one was resolved, so two installs a month apart can differ in whether they are vulnerable and neither is reproducible from what is committed.
findings.fix: Commit the lockfile, which fixes the resolution and makes this answerable.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Add a LICENSE; redistribution rights are undefined
findings.evidence: no licence file at the repository root
findings.why: With no licence the default is all rights reserved, so this code cannot legally be reused, which matters most for the owner's own work carried into client engagements.
findings.fix: Add MIT or Apache-2.0 at the repository root.

findings.title: Add a test suite; this repository has none
findings.why: Any change ships with no signal that existing behaviour still holds, so a regression reaches production undetected.
findings.fix: Add one test per public entry point, then a CI step that runs them.

findings.title: Add a workflow that builds and tests this repository
findings.why: Every change merges with nobody having run the build once, which across this estate is 499 repositories.
findings.fix: Add a workflow running the project build and test command on push and pull_request.

findings.title: Replace the wildcard CORS origin with an explicit allow list
findings.why: Any page on the internet can call the API with the browser's cookies attached, so a logged-in visitor to an unrelated site performs authenticated requests without knowing, and the wildcard combined with credentials is the exact configuration browsers refuse for that reason.
findings.fix: List the origins the API actually serves, and never pair a wildcard with credentials.

findings.title: Pin the container base image by digest
findings.why: An untagged or mutable base means today's build and last month's contain different libc and a different CVE set, with no record of which shipped.
findings.fix: Use image:tag@sha256:<digest> and enable Dependabot's docker ecosystem.

findings.title: Add a non-root USER to the image
findings.evidence: CMD or ENTRYPOINT with no USER directive
findings.why: A process running as root in the container is root against every mounted volume, and it turns any container escape or writable-mount mistake from a contained problem into a host one.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user, chown what it needs, and end the Dockerfile with USER.

findings.title: Give the outbound request a timeout
findings.why: requests has no default timeout, so a peer that accepts the connection and then says nothing holds the worker forever, and with a small worker pool a single slow dependency takes the whole service down without anything appearing to fail.
findings.fix: Pass timeout= on every call, or use a session with one configured.

findings.title: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a commit SHA
findings.why: A tag can be moved, so the action running with your token and secrets is whatever its owner last pushed; this is how tj-actions/changed-files leaked secrets from thousands of repos.
findings.fix: Replace each @vN with the 40-character commit SHA, keep # vN as a comment, and let Dependabot bump the SHAs.

findings.title: Commit a lockfile beside the manifest
findings.evidence: manifest with no lockfile in scope
findings.why: An unlocked range means the artifact you tested and the artifact you ship can contain different transitive code, so a malicious patch release reaches production with no diff.
findings.fix: Run the package manager once and commit the generated lockfile.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.evidence: 3 workflow(s) declare no permissions, 1 of them reference secrets
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.title: Keep secrets out of workflows a fork can trigger
findings.why: Contributor-controlled input reaches a job holding a publish token or cloud credential, so a pull request becomes credential exfiltration.
findings.fix: Move secret-using steps into a workflow_run job that never checks out pull request code, or gate on an environment with required reviewers.

findings.title: Pin the resolution so a vulnerable version cannot install
findings.evidence: no lockfile, and the declared ranges reach jupyterlab@4.0.0 CVE-2024-39700 (critical) +20 more; pyarrow@15.0.0 CVE-2026-25087 (critical) +2 more
findings.why: The range includes versions with published advisories and nothing in the repository records which one was resolved, so two installs a month apart can differ in whether they are vulnerable and neither is reproducible from what is committed.
findings.fix: Commit the lockfile, which fixes the resolution and makes this answerable.

findings.fix: Let the step fail, or test the specific expected condition instead of discarding all exit codes.

findings.title: Remove continue-on-error from steps that gate correctness
findings.why: A failing test suite reports a green check, which is precisely the path this audit exists to close.
findings.fix: Delete continue-on-error, or move a genuinely advisory step into a separate non-required job.

findings.title: Declare least-privilege permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN
findings.why: With no declaration the token inherits the repository default, so any injected step can push commits or mint releases from inside your own CI.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow and widen per job only where needed.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Gate pull requests on a dependency vulnerability scan
findings.why: This is the one gate that would catch a known-vulnerable package before it reaches a build, and no repository in the sample had it.
findings.fix: Add dependency-review-action on pull_request, or osv-scanner on push and a schedule.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository
findings.why: One repository here carries twenty blobs over 5MB including a 10.9MB spreadsheet, so every clone and every CI checkout pays for data nobody diffs.
findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
findings.fix: Add with: persist-credentials: false, and pass an explicit token only to the step that pushes.

findings.title: Expand the test suite; it cannot cover this codebase
findings.why: A reviewer reads "has tests" and assumes a safety net that covers two files out of eighty-five, which is how untested paths ship behind a green badge.
findings.fix: Add tests for the highest fan-in modules first.

findings.title: Set timeout-minutes on the workflow jobs
findings.why: A wedged step runs to the six-hour platform default, which on a two-hourly schedule means three runs overlap behind it.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes with a realistic bound to each job.

findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Upgrade the pinned dependency carrying a published advisory
findings.why: The pinned version is the one that installs, so a published advisory against it describes this deployment rather than a hypothetical one, and the advisory is also a public description of how to exploit it.
findings.fix: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory, then commit the lockfile.

findings.title: Enable Dependabot or Renovate
findings.why: Without a bot a published advisory sits unpatched until someone audits by hand, which across 1,322 repositories means never.
findings.fix: Commit .github/dependabot.yml covering the repo ecosystems plus github-actions.

findings.title: Move large binaries to Git LFS or out of the repository
findings.why: One repository here carries twenty blobs over 5MB including a 10.9MB spreadsheet, so every clone and every CI checkout pays for data nobody diffs.
findings.fix: Track those extensions with LFS, or move datasets to object storage and fetch them in a setup step.

findings.title: Pin the resolution so a vulnerable version cannot install
findings.evidence: no lockfile, and the declared ranges reach geopandas@0.10.0 CVE-2025-69662 (high) +1 more
findings.why: The range includes versions with published advisories and nothing in the repository records which one was resolved, so two installs a month apart can differ in whether they are vulnerable and neither is reproducible from what is committed.
findings.fix: Commit the lockfile, which fixes the resolution and makes this answerable.

findings.title: Add a LICENSE; redistribution rights are undefined
findings.evidence: no licence file at the repository root
findings.why: With no licence the default is all rights reserved, so this code cannot legally be reused, which matters most for the owner's own work carried into client engagements.
findings.fix: Add MIT or Apache-2.0 at the repository root.

findings.title: Add a workflow that builds and tests this repository
findings.why: Every change merges with nobody having run the build once, which across this estate is 499 repositories.
findings.fix: Add a workflow running the project build and test command on push and pull_request.

findings.title: Expand the test suite; it cannot cover this codebase
findings.why: A reviewer reads "has tests" and assumes a safety net that covers two files out of eighty-five, which is how untested paths ship behind a green badge.
findings.fix: Add tests for the highest fan-in modules first.

findings.title: Add the repository convention files this project lacks
findings.why: Without them one contributor's editor writes tabs into a Python file, a shell script commits with CRLF and fails in the container, and a notebook diff is unreviewable.
findings.fix: Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf, and a formatter config.

findings.title: Set persist-credentials: false on checkout
findings.evidence: checkout keeps the token, then dependencies are installed
findings.why: The token stays in .git/config for every later step, so a malicious postinstall script reads a pushable credential without one ever being passed to it.
